subject: MediQuant — follow-up: data handling options and pilot paths
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@mediquant.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap & immediate asks (data handling + pilot options)

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

- Scope: production inference for clinical triage ML workflows (low latency, PII in payloads: patient name, DOB, MRN, limited PHI)
- Must-haves from MediQuant: data residency in us-east-1, no long-term storage of patient identifiers, SOC2 evidence for our controls
- Asks we took away: confirm whether you need true 0-retention (no logs persisted) vs. shortened log window; any fields that must be redacted vs. hashed; procurement timeline (targeting Dec-2026 pilot)

Short-term options we can offer (to pick from):
1) Ephemeral/0-retention pilot: no request payloads written to disk; ephemeral KV cache during inference only; aggregate, anonymized metrics retained for SLOs. (Requires Dedicated or Private deployment.)
2) Short-window retention: non-PII logs retained for 24 hours; PII fields redacted at ingest; audit trails limited to anonymized traces.
3) Hybrid: KV cache kept for 6–24 hours for latency-sensitive endpoints; full request logs never persisted.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm which option you prefer (1, 2, or 3) and the exact PII/data elements that must be purged or redacted.
- Rafael/Laura can then propose the detailed control set and a proposed pilot runbook.
- If you want option 1, we need to confirm Dedicated/Private deployment requirement and timeline.

Attachments: I included the MediQuant privacy doc you shared in the thread for reference (received during the call).

I'll follow up with Rafael for feasibility notes and a proposed config by EOD Thursday (Nov 9).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & immediate asks (data handling + pilot options)

Marissa — appreciate the clear summary.

Quick answers:
- We are primarily concerned about patient identifiers (full name, DOB, MRN) and unstructured notes that may contain PHI. We would like those never to be stored in their original form.
- Goal is effectively "no persistent PII"; we are open to aggregated metrics for performance/availability.
- Procurement: we aim to sign a pilot agreement by mid-Dec if controls match our security team's requirements.

Can Redwood support an ephemeral mode where request payloads are not persisted anywhere (disk, object store) and only transiently held in memory/KV during inference? If so, what constraints (latency, model size, concurrency)?

I've attached our privacy requirements pdf for your security team to review.

—Ethan

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & immediate asks (data handling + pilot options)

Marissa — quick internal feasibility notes based on Ethan's ask:

Summary: We can support an "ephemeral mode" with caveats. High-level plan below.

Technical proposal:
- Ephemeral request handling: requests can be processed in-memory only with no write to durable storage. This requires Private or Dedicated infra (we cannot guarantee ephemeral guarantees on multi-tenant hosted instances due to shared storage hooks).
- KV cache: can be kept in-memory per instance; TTL configurable. For strict 0-retention we set KV TTL to 0s or disabled, but this may increase cold-start latency. A pragmatic default is a short TTL (e.g., 1–6 hours) to balance latency and privacy.
- Logs/audits: we can limit audit logs to anonymized traces (request ids, latency, error codes) with no request payload or PII. Operational metrics (tokens, latency percentiles) retained for 90 days by default but can be shortened to 30 days for the pilot.
- PII handling: we can offer a client-side redaction library (open-source) or server-side redaction at ingress (regex/field-mapping). Server-side redaction increases risk surface; recommend client-side hashing for MRNs.
- Encryption: TLS in transit; customer-managed KMS for keys at rest if using Private. For Dedicated, we can offer customer KMS integration.

Known constraints & tradeoffs:
- True 0-retention (no KV) will likely increase per-request latency for models that rely on KV for context. For pq-24 models we measured ~20–40% latency uplift without KV caching during bursts.
- Multi-region residency: we can pin to us-east-1 in Private/Dedicated. Hosted regions may have limited isolation guarantees.

Next actions:
- I will draft a short pilot runbook (config, SLOs, rollback) and a controls mapping to MediQuant's privacy doc.
- Need Ethan to confirm exact fields to redact vs. hash and whether client-side redaction is acceptable.

I'll attach our ephemeral ops note and network diagram for reference.

Rafael
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@mediquant.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Next steps & options — MediQuant pilot

Ethan — thanks. Based on Rafael's notes, two customer-facing options you can decide between:

Option A (Zero-persist pilot)
- Private or Dedicated deployment in us-east-1
- Ephemeral processing: no payloads written to disk; KV disabled or TTL=0
- No PII in logs; anonymized metrics only
- Expected latency: slightly higher for bursty workloads; we'll quantify in runbook

Option B (Short-window minimized logs)
- Hosted/Dedicated with KV TTL=24h (or configurable down to 6h)
- Server-side redaction or client-side hashing for MRN/DOB
- Non-PII operational logs retained 24–30 days; PII never persisted

Please confirm which you prefer. If Option A, we will schedule a technical deep-dive (security + infra) to align on deployment model and finalize the pilot contract. If Option B, we can proceed on Hosted Dedicated to expedite start.

Links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/view
- Shared draft runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e

I'll await your selection — happy to set the deep-dive for early next week.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@mediquant.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps & options — MediQuant pilot

Marissa — we will go with Option A (Zero-persist pilot) pending the runbook and SOC2 evidence. Can Rafael share the SOC2 / controls mapping and the ephemeral ops note you mentioned? Also confirm whether Private deployment is required for Option A or if Dedicated with customer KMS is sufficient for our legal team.

Let's schedule the technical deep-dive on Monday Nov 9, 10:00am PT if that works for your team.

—Ethan
